subject.title: [Feature]: TUI: vi/vim keybinding mode for input editor

question: Should vi/vim modal editing be built into OpenClaw's TUI, delegated to pi-tui/editor support, or exposed through a plugin/editor extension seam first?
rationale: The user need is clear, but the closed companion PR and repository config-surface policy leave the permanent owner boundary and public configuration shape unresolved.

options.title: Upstream/editor seam first
options.body: Keep this issue as the product/API decision and avoid core vi config until pi-tui or a real OpenClaw editor-extension seam can own full modal behavior.

options.title: Core default-off vi mode
options.body: Accept a scoped OpenClaw CustomEditor implementation with explicit limitations, config docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: ClawHub package path
options.body: Close core implementation once a working editor seam exists and ask for the vi editor to ship as a plugin/package instead.

recommendation.title: Upstream/editor seam first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the product/API decision and avoid core vi config until pi-tui or a real OpenClaw editor-extension seam can own full modal behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant TUI and pi-tui integration history points most strongly to steipete for the editor ownership decision.
